digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### Google says criminal hackers used AI to find a major software flaw
URL: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/11/us/politics/google-hackers-attack-ai.html
AI-assisted vulnerability discovery has crossed from theoretical to operational.
This is the inflection point security researchers warned about — attackers now have the same force multiplier that defenders use. Expect vulnerability discovery timelines to compress significantly, which changes the economics of zero-day markets and puts pressure on patch cycles across the industry.

### Postmortem: TanStack NPM supply-chain compromise
URL: https://tanstack.com/blog/npm-supply-chain-compromise-postmortem
Supply chain attacks hit one of JavaScript's most trusted libraries.
TanStack powers routing and state management for millions of React apps. This postmortem will be required reading for anyone evaluating open-source dependency risk. The attack surface of modern software — where a single maintainer's credentials can compromise thousands of production systems — remains fundamentally unsolved.

### Expat 2.8.1 released, CVE-2026-45186 and CVSS unreliability
URL: https://blog.hartwork.org/posts/expat-2-8-1-released/
XML parsing library patches critical flaw; maintainers flag CVSS scoring as broken.
Expat is embedded in Python, Apache, and countless enterprise stacks. The meta-story here — that CVSS scores are becoming unreliable signals for prioritization — matters for anyone building vulnerability management programs or compliance tooling.


## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### Daniel Ek-backed defense tech Helsing to raise $1.2B at $18B valuation
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/11/daniel-ek-backed-defense-tech-helsing-to-raise-1-2b-at-18b-valuation/
European defense AI hits unicorn scale in under five years.
Helsing's trajectory — from founding to $18B — tracks the structural shift of defense procurement toward autonomous systems. The Spotify founder's involvement signals continued crossover of consumer tech capital into defense. Watch for consolidation plays as legacy contractors respond.

### Venmo's biggest makeover in years comes at a very interesting time
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/11/venmos-biggest-makeover-in-years-comes-at-a-very-interesting-time/
PayPal dresses Venmo for sale as Stripe circles.
The restructuring into a standalone unit is textbook pre-divestiture positioning. Stripe acquiring Venmo would create a consumer-to-merchant payments stack with serious network effects. This is the fintech M&A story to watch — valuations, regulatory hurdles, and strategic rationale are all live variables.

### Korea's biggest manufacturers back Config, the TSMC of robot data
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/11/koreas-biggest-manufacturers-back-config-the-tsmc-of-robot-data/
Hyundai, Samsung, and LG bet on training data as the bottleneck for robotics.
The "TSMC of robot data" framing is aggressive but instructive — Config is positioning data curation as the foundational layer, not hardware or algorithms. Korean industrial backing suggests serious intent to compete with US robotics plays. Data moats in physical AI could be stickier than in software.

### GM just laid off hundreds of IT workers to hire those with stronger AI skills
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/11/gm-just-laid-off-hundreds-of-it-workers-to-hire-those-with-stronger-ai-skills/
Legacy auto accelerates workforce composition shift toward AI-native roles.
This isn't a cost cut — it's a swap. GM is explicitly trading traditional IT headcount for prompt engineers and agent developers. The signal: incumbents are internalizing that AI competency is strategic, not a vendor relationship. Talent arbitrage opportunities exist for firms moving faster than hiring cycles.


## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### If AI writes your code, why use Python?
URL: https://medium.com/@NMitchem/if-ai-writes-your-code-why-use-python-bf8c4ba1a055
AI-generated code reopens the language selection conversation.
If human readability matters less than machine generation and execution efficiency, the calculus shifts toward compiled languages. This is an early-stage thesis, but one worth tracking — it could reshape which languages win in AI-native development environments over the next cycle.

### Zig vs Rust in 2026
URL: https://zackoverflow.dev/writing/zig-vs-rust-in-2026/
Systems programming language competition intensifies as both mature.
Rust has captured mindshare, but Zig's simplicity and C interop are gaining traction for specific use cases. For PE, the downstream signal is toolchain fragmentation — portfolio companies making systems-level bets need clear language strategy or risk technical debt accumulation.

### There aren't enough rockets for space data centers — Cowboy Space raised $275M to build them
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/11/there-arent-enough-rockets-for-space-data-centers-cowboy-space-raised-275-million-to-build-them/
Space compute demand outpaces launch capacity; new entrant raises at scale.
The $275M raise prices in real demand for orbital compute, not just hype. The constraint isn't silicon or cooling — it's launch vehicles. Watch whether SpaceX responds with dedicated capacity or if vertical integration becomes necessary for space datacenter players.


## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The through-line today is infrastructure scarcity meeting AI acceleration — whether it's rockets for space compute, training data for robots, or qualified humans for legacy enterprises. Security is getting harder as AI democratizes offense. The interesting capital flows are into picks-and-shovels plays (data, launch capacity, talent) rather than end applications. Stripe/PayPal and defense tech valuations suggest we're mid-cycle on consolidation in fintech and early-cycle on defense AI — position accordingly.
